answer: Each new identity must answer a peer-issued micro-benchmark: a random verifier publishes a task with a 90-second wall-clock deadline, and the claimant returns a signed trace hash at the vertex of a fixed compute graph. Because the deadline forbids batching, a clone farm cannot share one GPU across thousands of keys; each claim needs its own live silicon pulse, measured in 1.2 TFLOPs of unique work. On timeout or mismatched hash the stake scatters like sand off a dune, forfeiting $4.75 per attempt, so 50,000 sockpuppets cost $237,500 before casting a single valid vote.
